links.outcome: Authenticity and accuracy of citations in LLM-generated versus human-authored clinical reviews
links.effect: LLM-generated reviews had fewer references, less comprehensive insights, lower logical consistency, and lower authenticity and accuracy in their citations; more references came from lower-tier journals. No numbers in the abstract.
links.quote: This study presents a systematic comparison between LLM-generated and human-authored clinical reviews, revealing that while AI can quickly produce reviews, it often has fewer references, less comprehensive insights, and lower logical consistency while exhibiting lower authenticity and accuracy in their citations.

links.outcome: Ability of current detection systems to identify AI-generated review content
links.effect: Current detection systems were inefficient at identifying AI-generated content; no numbers in the abstract.
links.quote: Moreover, the study uncovers a concerning inefficiency in current detection systems for identifying AI-generated content, suggesting a need for more advanced checking systems and a stronger ethical framework to ensure academic transparency.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation comparing LLM-generated vs human-authored clinical literature reviews for evidence synthesis, focusing on quality, citation accuracy, and detection efficiency.
